title.rendered: Sunderland and Newcastle to join GBGB seeding pilot scheme

content.rendered:
The Greyhound Board of Great Britain (GBGB) has confirmed that Sunderland and Newcastle will join its seeding pilot scheme from 1 November.

The pilot was introduced on 21 September at Romford, Sheffield Stadium and Towcester Racecourse, with GBGB stating at its launch that there was an intention to extend the scheme to additional racecourses as the trial progressed.

The scheme is trialling an additional Rails to Middle seeding category alongside the established seeding options, providing an additional classification for greyhounds when race draws are made.

The inclusion of Sunderland and Newcastle represents the next stage in the pilot as GBGB continues to assess the use of the additional seeding option across participating racecourses.

title.rendered: Shadow Storm Chases Scurry Gold Cup History at Dunstall Park

content.rendered:
SHADOW STORM has a chance to become just the fourth greyhound to win back-to-back Scurry Gold Cups when he lines up in Saturday’s £12,500-to-the-winner Arena Racing Company-backed sprinters’ showpiece at Dunstall Park.

On a night the track at Wolverhampton Racecourse is also staging the Premier Greyhound Racing Oaks Final for a huge double-header, Richard Rees’ champion two-bend performer, the reigning GBGB Sprinter of the Year, lines up as one of two finalists for the Hove trainer in a competition which has been upgraded back to Category One status this year.

“Well done to all for making it a Cat One. It’s back to where it always should have been,” said Rees. “So hats off to Dunstall Park. I know their racing manager Martin Seal was keen to get it back up there and we know he’s a great supporter of what we’re doing. He introduced the Dunstall Dash this year for the sprinters, too.”

Dunstall Park have been rewarded with a brilliant final and Rees understands only the best will do from both of his runners and is happy heading into the final.

“Look, we all know about sprints. There are fine margins and you can lose it in a split second unlike four and six bends when you’ve got a chance to recover. In a field of six brilliant sprinters we know only the best will do – for any of them.

“Of course it’d be nice to defend the title and he’s a greyhound who owes us nothing. He’s got a chance, but so, too, has Avarua Lake. He’s always been in the shadow of Storm as such, but is a very fast dog in his own right. We’re looking forward to it.”

Avarua Lake raced into the lead round the first bend in last week’s first semi-final when leading home Arc Silver Salver winner Ballinakill Liam (Mark Wallis) by a length in 15.86sec (-5), before Michelle Brown’s prolific-scoring Roanna Mamba edged out Magical Jason (Kevin Hutton) in the second semi-final, stopping the clock in 15.73sec (-50.

The third and final semi-final went to the Rees-trained Shadow Storm who set the standard when hitting the front between the first and second turns before drawing away for a length and a quarter success over Newinn Souly in 15.66sec (-5).

title.rendered: Upcoming Webinar – Lungworm in Greyhounds: What Every Trainer Needs to Know

content.rendered:
Tuesday 8 December 2026 | 12:00–13:00 | Online via Microsoft Teams

Join us for our next free GBGB webinar, focusing on lungworm and the proactive steps trainers can take to protect the health and wellbeing of their greyhounds. Lungworm is an emerging and potentially life-threatening disease, making early detection and prevention essential.

This webinar will be led by Professor Hany Elsheikha, Professor of Interdisciplinary Parasitology at the University of Nottingham and a leading expert in parasitology.

The session will provide practical information and advice for those caring for greyhounds, covering:

  • What lungworm is and why greyhounds may be at risk.
  • Clinical signs and early warning indicators.
  • Diagnosis and treatment options.
  • Prevention and parasite control programmes.
  • Practical management advice.

 

The webinar is free to attend, and all GBGB licence holders are encouraged to join. A Q&A will follow the presentation.

Register for your place

To register, please email Meriel France, GBGB Learning and Development Manager, at meriel.france@gbgb.org.uk.

This webinar forms part of GBGB’s ongoing education programme, helping GBGB licence holders stay up to date with the latest research and developments in greyhound welfare and care. Keep an eye on the GBGB calendar for details of upcoming online and in-person events.

title.rendered: Signet Nayla Chases Oaks Glory as Hutton Targets Dunstall Park Double

content.rendered:
KEVIN HUTTON has extra reason for looking forward to Saturday’s major double-header at Dunstall Park after both Signet Nayla and Magical Jason respectively made the finals of the Premier Greyhound Racing Oaks and Arena Racing Company Scurry Gold Cup.

For Signet Nayla, the weekend’s £20,000 contest for the bitches’ Classic decider is a second consecutive Category One final at Wolverhampton Racecourse for the British-bred after running-up to Woltemade in the Arena Racing Company Birmingham Cup last month.

“She’s been running really well,” said Hutton after the home-bred April 2023 daughter of Signet Denver and Not Too Late unleashed her trademark burst of early pace to win the first semi-final of the Oaks, crossing the line a length and a half clear of the running-on Strike It Skye (Mark Wallis) in 28.35sec (-10).

“I thought she ran a cracker against Jimmy’s (Fenwick) dog in the Birmingham Cup and just gives herself a chance by breaking well – and that’s what we’re hoping for on Saturday in what is a brilliant Oaks final. We’ve the best bitches in the UK and Graham (Holland) bringing a good team over from Ireland and getting two through only adds to it. 

“It looks one of the best we’ve had for a while and, of course, everyone knows how much we love the Oaks. It’s where everything really did step up for us a notch when Droopys Danneel won at Belle Vue in 2013. Seems a lifetime ago now – and it is!”

Signet Nayla led off the second bend in the first semi-final on her way to winning by a length and quarter from Strike It Skye (Mark Wallis) who ran on strongly to edge Ballymac Allory (Esther Driver) for second to secure a place in Saturday’s £20,000 final. The winning time for Signet Nayla was 28.35sec (-10).

The other semi-finals went to Graham Holland’s Irish raider Fahrenheit Jess who made all to clock a fastest-of-the-round 27.87sec (-10) from Holding Hollie (Richie Taberner) and Brian Fairbairn’s Slingshot Poppy whose trademark burst of early pace set the seal on a 27.90sec (-10) success over Ballydoyle Tina (Graham Holland) in 27.90sec (-10).

title.rendered: Returning Storm Sets the Pace as Doncaster Puppy Derby Roars into Life

content.rendered:
DONCASTER racing official Stephen Gray was really impressed by the overall quality of the youngsters on show as the Doncaster Puppy Derby kicked off on Saturday – with Romford raider Returning Storm quickest of the heat winners. 

The David Mullins-trained pup raced away to a 27.49sec (-10) success in heat five of the 450m Category One event at the South Yorkshire venue which completed a good night for the Romford trainer as his Shado Earth won the previous heat in 27.69sec (-10), initiating a double for the Essex-based team.

The event had kicked off with another nod to Romford form with success for Carrigoon Cece as Michelle Brown’s youngster, the Coral Romford Puppy Cup winner, raced away early for a five and a half lengths success in 27.55sec (-10).

Other heat winners were the Yarmouth-based pair of Mark Brighton’s Frankton Grange in 27.73sec (-10) and Craig Morris’s Lady Gambet in 27.66sec (-10), and Samantha Lapidge’s local hope Cockneys Zachery in 28.25sec (-10).

Gray said: “We were delighted with the overall quality of the Puppy Derby entry and that was borne out with some impressive performances in the heats. Trainers have travelled distances with their greyhounds to get here which is a real thumbs-up to the track and what we are doing here – and for the competition itself.

“There were a few eye-catchers,” added Gray. “David’s (Mullins) team is clearly a good one and his two brothers – Shado Earth and War Hound – look pretty closely matched. Shado Earth won his heat well and War Hound was a good second to Frankton Grange. Both will improve. David also has another nice sort in Returning Storm, of course. He ran in what was the toughest of the heats, so that performance cannot be underestimated.

“Carrigoon Cece blasted out and was soon clear in front in the opening heat to uphold the Romford Puppy Cup form, while Lady Gambet looks a strong bitch with a great will-to-win, and, while it was the slowest heat time, seeing one of our own in Cockneys Zachery come through to win the most exciting heat to watch was great to see.

“We’re now all looking forward to Saturday’s semi-finals and the final a week later.”

title.rendered: Adelinesfirstdog Delivers Steel City Cup Glory as Sheffield Hails BetGoodwin Partnership

content.rendered:
ANDREW MASCARENHAS, director of racing at Sheffield’s Owlerton Stadium, has thanked BetGoodwin for stepping into sponsor the Steel City Cup, the South Yorkshire track’s biggest event of the year which concluded with victory last weekend for the Richie Taberner-trained Adelinesfirstdog. 

Mascarenhas said: “BetGoodwin were great from start to finish and hopefully this year’s event is just the start of a great partnership between us and them. Their boss Julian Head didn’t quite manage to take away the trophy with him but his Grouchos Cossie ran a really good race in defeat it should be said. 

“It was a competitive competition overall, finishing with a cracking final – and perhaps a surprise result for most judges in Adelinesfirstdog winning.

“He was the outsider of the field but claimed a famous win in this year’s BetGoodwin Steel City Cup. 

“One of three runners for Richie Taberner’s kennel, he was able to match likely Greyhound of the Year Woltemade round the first bend before proving his class to win the final with just under five lengths separating the entire field.

“It capped a great day for Richie who had four winners that afternoon.

“Thanks go to all entries in this year’s competition and, once again, to BetGoodwin for stepping in support our major Cat One competition here.”

Going off the 110-10 favourite, four-time Category One winner Woltemade (Jimmy Fenwick) made the best start outside and looked set to go round in front until the pace of Adelinesfirstdog saw the Monmore raider range up inside the Newcastle tracker and forged ahead off the second bend. 

Always in front thereafter, the heavyweight September 2024 Dromana Bucko and Ellie O kept up the gallop and was never headed for a three-length win from kennelmate Moanteen Hatton for a Taberner one-two in 28.86sec (normal).

The winner, named after owner Keith Moores’s granddaughter, took home the £12,500 first prize for a second Taberner-trained Category One winner in the space of weeks after Countess Penny’s Produce Stakes win at Towcester.

title.rendered: Annadown Warrior Fires Locke Further Clear in Trainer of the Year battle with Kent Derby Triumph

content.rendered:
ANNADOWN WARRIOR helped extend Maxine Locke’s lead at the top of the Trainer of the Year standings with victory in the final of the Premier Greyhound Racing Kent Derby at Central Park on Saturday.

Central Park handler Locke (1016), landing her second Kent Derby victory after Droopys Display’s success in 2024, burst through the 1,000 barrier courtesy of this latest Category One triumph and has a significant advantage over Paul Young (850) and Mark Wallis (809) – and Locke herself is thrilled to have notched another big-race success.

“It’s brilliant for Jo (Ramsay, assistant) and the team who are doing an amazing job,” said Locke. “Warrior is just a fantastic young dog and has shown himself to be top class with two Cat One wins on his record now and we’ll probably now aim him at Nottingham again.

“He won the Puppy Classic there and broke the track record so the (PGR) Eclipse seems the right option.”

Of the final itself, Locke added: “He took his chance well when things opened up. You knew in such a top-class final, probably the best we’ve seen this year bar the Towcester Derby final maybe, he’d have to do things right – that meant just missing the break slightly! That’s probably helped him when they crowded at the turn.

“I’m delighted for Jack (Russell) and the whole JR Racing Syndicate. The likes of Jack, Dean (Goldfinch) and Adam (Williams), plus dad of course, are great supporters of what we do at Bonville Kennels and thank you to them for their continued support.”

Annadown Warrior had been led from the boxes by both Proper Heiress (Mark Wallis), the GBGB Greyhound of the Year and track record holder, and Scooby The Lady (Richard Rees), who previously held the record. However, when that pair came together at the turn, Locke’s runner was best placed to hit the front off the second bend.

Always in charge thereafter, the September 2024 son of Grangeview Ten and Annadown Cutie, a member of a hugely talented and big-race winning litter, kept up the pace to cross the line in front of Scooby Mustang (Carol Weatherall), the latter running on really well to get within half a length of the 28.85sec (normal) winner.

Third home was Proper Heiress, just ahead of the unlucky ARC Select Stakes champion Underground Gold (Paul Young), but the £20,000 prize was Annadown Warrior’s.

title.rendered: Category One Glory Beckons in Coral 100 Champion Stakes Final

content.rendered:
ROMFORD is building up to its last Category One final of 2026 with the Coral 100 Champion Stakes coming to a conclusion over 575m on Friday.

In a week in which the London Road venue will be featured again on The Box Seat, Sky Sports Racing’s brand new greyhound show, on Wednesday, Romford’s communications manager Jess Day knows she and the team, led by stadium manager Karen McMillan, have another busy week ahead of them.

“We’re really looking forward to the Coral 100 Champion Stakes Final on Friday, with it being our biggest Cat One of the year, worth £20,000 to the winner – and dedicating it to 100 years of Coral which makes it even more special,” said Day.

“We were all gutted to see Newinn Jolly withdrawn and feel for connections, but welfare must come first so we are wishing him the best and look forward to seeing him back at London Road again soon,” added Day of the news that a urine infection has ruled out Kim Billingham’s runner from a crack at the showpiece final.

“It’s certainly all go at Romford in preparation for Friday,” continued Day. “Little touches like balloons, photo frames, rosettes, chocolates, pens – and more – make the difference, and all very worth it to make the night that bit more memorable. It’s going to be a great final and we look forward to welcoming everyone – hounds and people alike!”

Fastest semi-final winner was the Kelly Wilton-trained Grouchos Gregor who raced to an all-the-way victory in the third semi-final, leading home Fortanach Col for a brilliant one-two for the Nottingham trainer. The winning time was 35.36sec (-20), with the runner-up now eyeing a third Category One success after scoring wins in both the Time 3 Steps To Victory at Sheffield and Ladbrokes Summer Stayers Classic at Monmore.

The other semi-finals were won by the Paul Young-trained Bubbly Holly who led home the unfortunate Newinn Jolly (Kim Billingham-Hine) in the first semi in 35.95sec (-20) and the John Mullins-trained Aayamza Legend in 35.75sec (-20), the latter crossing the line clear of Don Cici (David Mullins) in the second semi.

title.rendered: Trainer of the Year standings – up to and including Sunday 18th October

content.rendered:
Maxine Locke tightened her grip on the Trainers’ Championship with another outstanding week, adding 72 points to become the first trainer to break through the 1,000-point barrier on 1,016.

While P W Young remains in pursuit on 850, the championship leader has stretched her advantage to 166 points and looks increasingly difficult to reel in.

The foundations for Locke’s latest surge were laid during a sensational Saturday night at Central Park, where her kennel dominated proceedings with four winners, headed by Annadown Warrior’s impressive success in the Kent Derby. It was a statement performance from the championship front-runner and one that further underlined the strength and depth behind her title challenge.

Standout performer

No trainer made a bigger statement this week than Richie Taberner. A sensational 94-point return propelled Taberner four places up the standings from 14th to 10th, with his total climbing to 387 points. In a week of significant movement throughout the table, Taberner’s charge was the standout performance, vaulting him into the top ten and adding fresh intrigue to the championship race.
